title: Happy or sad What type of music do you like
titleChinese: 你喜欢悲伤还是快乐的音乐？
paragraphs: What would life be like without music? Songs and tunes fill our lives, affecting our emotions, bringing back memories and sometimes making us dance. There is a song for everyone and for every occasion, but it seems that it’s sad music that moves us most.

Sad music certainly does its job in making us depressed, emotional, and causing us to sob – it’s something we might listen to after a break-up, for example. And a recent study has shown why some people are hooked on sad music. Professor David Huron from Ohio State University conducted the research and looked at the difference between people who love to listen to sad music and those who can’t stand it.

He told the BBC radio programme The Why Factor that it comes down to a natural hormone called prolactin. He says: “as you might have guessed from the name, it's associated with ‘lactation’ from breast-feeding. When people cry, they also release prolactin. And, there are circumstances in which prolactin seems to have this comforting effect.” It seems that people who like sad music are maybe getting too much prolactin, or more than is normal, and when they hear sad, downbeat music, it gives them a good feeling. But if prolactin isn’t released, or there isn’t enough of it, some people find the sad sounds don’t help to cheer them up.

Previous research by Durham University has also suggested that listening to sad music can trigger pain and sadness; but it can also provide comfort and even enjoyment. A high number of people they surveyed were cheered up by listening to supposedly sad songs. Though the feeling may not be exactly the same as happiness, it may be the ability to cope with the sadness that gives the feeling of comfort.

So, reacting to sad music on the radio may have nothing to do with the melancholic sound of a string quartet or a singer who’s got the blues, but rather a natural chemical reaction taking place in our bodies. Maybe that explanation is music to your ears if you're wondering why you’ve been listening to Adele on repeat!

vocabulary.entry: hooked on /hʊkt ɒn/ 沉迷于；对……上瘾
vocabulary.example: She's hooked on classical music and listens to it every night.
vocabulary.translation: 她沉迷于古典音乐，每晚都听。

vocabulary.entry: prolactin /prəʊˈlæktɪn/ n. 催乳素（一种激素）
vocabulary.example: Prolactin levels rise during pregnancy to prepare for breastfeeding.
vocabulary.translation: 怀孕期间催乳素水平会升高，为哺乳做准备。

vocabulary.entry: lactation /lækˈteɪʃn/ n. 泌乳；哺乳
vocabulary.example: The book offers advice on lactation and infant feeding.
vocabulary.translation: 这本书提供了关于泌乳和婴儿喂养的建议。

vocabulary.entry: release /rɪˈliːs/ v. 释放；排放
vocabulary.example: Exercise helps the body release endorphins, which reduce stress.
vocabulary.translation: 运动有助于身体释放内啡肽，从而减轻压力。

vocabulary.entry: comforting effect /ˈkʌmfətɪŋ ɪˈfekt/ 安慰效果；慰藉作用
vocabulary.example: Her mother's voice had a comforting effect on her when she was upset.
vocabulary.translation: 她难过时，妈妈的声音能给她带来安慰。

vocabulary.entry: downbeat /ˈdaʊnbiːt/ adj. 低沉的；悲观的
vocabulary.example: The song has a downbeat melody that reflects the singer's mood.
vocabulary.translation: 这首歌的旋律低沉，反映了歌手的心情。

vocabulary.entry: trigger /ˈtrɪɡə(r)/ v. 引发；触发
vocabulary.example: Certain smells can trigger memories of childhood.
vocabulary.translation: 特定的气味能勾起童年的回忆。

vocabulary.entry: cope with /kəʊp wɪð/ 应对；处理
vocabulary.example: It's important to learn how to cope with stress in daily life.
vocabulary.translation: 学会在日常生活中应对压力很重要。

vocabulary.entry: melancholic /ˌmelənˈkɒlɪk/ adj. 忧郁的；悲伤的
vocabulary.example: The painting has a melancholic atmosphere that touches the viewer.
vocabulary.translation: 这幅画有一种忧郁的氛围，打动了观者。

vocabulary.entry: string quartet /strɪŋ kwɔːˈtet/ 弦乐四重奏（由两把小提琴、一把中提琴和一把大提琴组成）
vocabulary.example: We went to a concert featuring a famous string quartet.
vocabulary.translation: 我们去听了一场著名弦乐四重奏的音乐会。

vocabulary.entry: got the blues /ɡɒt ðə bluːz/ 心情忧郁；感到伤感（口语）
vocabulary.example: He's got the blues because he didn't get the job he wanted.
vocabulary.translation: 他因为没得到想要的工作而心情低落。

vocabulary.entry: chemical reaction /ˈkemɪkl riˈækʃn/ 化学反应
vocabulary.example: Photosynthesis is a complex chemical reaction that occurs in plants.
vocabulary.translation: 光合作用是植物体内发生的复杂化学反应。

vocabulary.entry: on repeat /ɒn rɪˈpiːt/ 反复循环播放（口语）
vocabulary.example: I've had that song on repeat all morning—it's so catchy.
vocabulary.translation: 我一早上都在反复循环那首歌，它太朗朗上口了。

vocabulary.entry: music to your ears /ˈmjuːzɪk tu jɔː(r) ɪəz/ 悦耳的话；中听的消息（习语）
vocabulary.example: The news that we'd won the contract was music to our ears.
vocabulary.translation: 我们赢得合同的消息让我们喜出望外。

vocabulary.entry: sob /sɒb/ v. 啜泣；抽噎
vocabulary.example: She couldn't help sobbing when she heard the sad news.
vocabulary.translation: 听到这个悲伤的消息，她忍不住啜泣起来。

vocabulary.entry: break-up /ˈbreɪk ʌp/ n. 分手；关系破裂
vocabulary.example: He found it hard to cope with the break-up of his relationship.
vocabulary.translation: 他很难接受恋情的破裂。

vocabulary.entry: can’t stand /kɑːnt stænd/ 无法忍受；受不了
vocabulary.example: I can't stand loud music—it gives me a headache.
vocabulary.translation: 我受不了嘈杂的音乐，它会让我头疼。

vocabulary.entry: come down to /kʌm daʊn tu/ 归结为；归根结底是
vocabulary.example: The success of the project comes down to careful planning and teamwork.
vocabulary.translation: 这个项目的成功归根结底在于精心规划和团队合作。

vocabulary.entry: cheer up /tʃɪə(r) ʌp/ 使振作；使高兴起来
vocabulary.example: 我心情低落时，去公园散步总能让我振作起来。
vocabulary.translation: A walk in the park always cheers me up when I'm feeling low.

vocabulary.entry: supposedly /səˈpəʊzɪdli/ adv. 据称；按理说
vocabulary.example: The film is supposedly based on a true story.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影据称是基于真实故事改编的。

vocabulary.entry: emotional /ɪˈməʊʃənl/ adj. 情绪激动的；易动感情的
vocabulary.example: She's a very emotional person and cries easily at sad movies.
vocabulary.translation: 她是个非常重感情的人，看悲伤的电影很容易哭。

vocabulary.entry: tunes /tjuːnz/ n. 旋律；曲调
vocabulary.example: He hummed some familiar tunes while he worked.
vocabulary.translation: 他工作时哼着一些熟悉的旋律。

sentences.english: What would life be like without music?
sentences.chinese: 没有音乐的人生会是什么样子？

sentences.english: Songs and tunes fill our lives, affecting our emotions, bringing back memories and sometimes making us dance.
sentences.chinese: 歌曲和旋律使我们生活更加充实，影响着我们的情绪，唤醒回忆，有时还会让我们翩翩起舞。

sentences.english: There is a song for everyone and for every occasion, but it seems that it’s sad music that moves us most.
sentences.chinese: 每个人、每个场合都有对应的歌曲，但似乎最能打动我们的，是悲伤的音乐。

sentences.english: Sad music certainly does its job in making us depressed, emotional, and causing us to sob – it’s something we might listen to after a break-up, for example.
sentences.chinese: 悲伤的音乐确实能起到让我们情绪低落、心生感触、甚至潸然泪下的作用——比如，分手后我们可能就会听这类音乐。

sentences.english: And a recent study has shown why some people are hooked on sad music.
sentences.chinese: 最近一项研究揭示了有些人沉迷悲伤音乐的原因。

sentences.english: Professor David Huron from Ohio State University conducted the research and looked at the difference between people who love to listen to sad music and those who can’t stand it.
sentences.chinese: 俄亥俄州立大学的大卫·休伦教授开展了这项研究，探究了热爱悲伤音乐与无法忍受悲伤音乐的人群之间的差异。

sentences.english: He told the BBC radio programme The Why Factor that it comes down to a natural hormone called prolactin. He says: “as you might have guessed from the name, it's associated with ‘lactation’ from breast-feeding.
sentences.chinese: 他在接受BBC广播节目《原因何在》（The Why Factor）采访时表示，这归根结底与一种名为催乳素（prolactin）的天然激素有关。

sentences.english: When people cry, they also release prolactin.
sentences.chinese: 他说：“从名字你可能就能猜到，它与母乳喂养中的‘泌乳’有关。

sentences.english: And, there are circumstances in which prolactin seems to have this comforting effect.”
sentences.chinese: 人们哭泣时也会释放催乳素，而且在某些情况下，催乳素似乎能产生这种安慰效果。”

sentences.english: It seems that people who like sad music are maybe getting too much prolactin, or more than is normal, and when they hear sad, downbeat music, it gives them a good feeling.
sentences.chinese: 喜欢悲伤音乐的人，体内的催乳素可能过多或超出正常水平，当他们听到悲伤、低沉的音乐时，会产生愉悦感。

sentences.english: But if prolactin isn’t released, or there isn’t enough of it, some people find the sad sounds don’t help to cheer them up.
sentences.chinese: 但如果催乳素没有被释放，或者含量不足，有些人就会觉得悲伤的音乐无法让他们振作起来。

sentences.english: Previous research by Durham University has also suggested that listening to sad music can trigger pain and sadness; but it can also provide comfort and even enjoyment.
sentences.chinese: 杜伦大学此前的一项研究也表明，听悲伤的音乐可能会引发痛苦和悲伤情绪，但同时也能带来安慰，甚至愉悦感。

sentences.english: A high number of people they surveyed were cheered up by listening to supposedly sad songs.
sentences.chinese: 他们调查发现，很多人听了本应悲伤的歌曲后反而心情变好。

sentences.english: Though the feeling may not be exactly the same as happiness, it may be the ability to cope with the sadness that gives the feeling of comfort.
sentences.chinese: 这种感觉或许与幸福感并不完全相同，但可能正是这种应对悲伤的能力，让人产生了舒适感。

sentences.english: So, reacting to sad music on the radio may have nothing to do with the melancholic sound of a string quartet or a singer who’s got the blues, but rather a natural chemical reaction taking place in our bodies.
sentences.chinese: 因此，我们对电台里悲伤音乐的反应，或许与弦乐四重奏的忧郁旋律或歌手的伤感唱腔无关，而是源于我们体内发生的一种自然化学反应。

sentences.english: Maybe that explanation is music to your ears if you're wondering why you’ve been listening to Adele on repeat!
sentences.chinese: 如果你正疑惑自己为什么会反复循环阿黛尔的歌曲，这个解释或许会让你豁然开朗！
